pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Good morning, home town! Sun, sand and the sound of cards being shuffled.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Today is the Festival of the Palms. Everyone is outside, but nobody is dueling.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: They are all whispering. Something is going on. I'll write it in my notebook.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Ask Teana, Jono and the Guard what the whispers are about.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: {name}! Come here, quick! You won't believe what happened at dawn.

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: A man in a black hood bought my whole tray of date cakes!

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: That's great news! Why the long face?

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: He paid with THIS. A golden star! He said 'See you in the Kingdom' and left.

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: And there were no footprints in the sand. Not one!

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A hooded man pays with golden stars and talks about a Kingdom.
pages.label: Rumor 1

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Ask Jono and the Guard too. Everybody knows a different piece!

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Three rumors, one mystery! Old Simon knows old stories. Go and ask him.

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: Hey, {name}! Perfect timing. I'm about to become rich and famous!

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Again? Last week it was the sand-surfing business.

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: This is different! A sailor told me about a white ship by the river mouth.

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: It sails to an island where duelists fight for stars. The winner gets ANYTHING!

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: Anything! Even a lifetime supply of fried fish!

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A white ship takes duelists to an island. Winners get anything.
pages.label: Rumor 2

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: Don't tell anyone, but I'm already packing. Heh. Go ask the others.

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: Simon will know what this is about. Old men always do. Go on, I'll wait.

pages.speaker: guard
pages.text: Halt! Oh, it's you, {name}. Keep your voice down.

pages.speaker: guard
pages.text: Last night someone nailed a poster to the gate. Strange paper. It glowed.

pages.speaker: guard
pages.text: I tore it down, as is my job. But the wind took half of it. Look.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: 'STAR PASSAGE. Three treasures. One duelist.' And then it's torn off.

pages.speaker: guard
pages.text: That's all I know. Ask old Simon. He gets nervous when people say 'Kingdom'.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A torn poster says - Star Passage. Three treasures. One duelist.
pages.label: Rumor 3

pages.speaker: guard
pages.text: I told you what I know. Talk to the others, but quietly.

pages.speaker: guard
pages.text: Simon. Go and see Simon. And never say I showed you that poster.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: The village notice board. 'Date harvest on Friday. Lost goat - answers to Sphinx.'

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Under it, a shiny gold nail. Someone pinned something here last night.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Still just a goat notice and a gold nail. The goat is probably fine.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: The whole village buzzes like bees. I prefer quiet.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: Ask Teana, Jono and the Guard what they heard. Then come and tell me.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: {name}! You look like someone carrying three rumors.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: A hooded man, a white ship and a torn poster. Simon, what is the Kingdom?

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: Hm. Nobody has said that word in this village for thirty years.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: I will tell you. But first show me you can hold a deck without shaking. Duel?

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: Steady hands and a good heart. Good. Now listen carefully.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: Far across the sea lies Duelist Kingdom, an island castle built by a showman named Pegasus.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: Duelists gather there with star chips. Win a duel and take a star. Lose and you give one.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: Ten stars open the castle gates. Whoever reaches the top faces Pegasus himself.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: And the winner gets anything?

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: Anything he asks. That is the bait. Pegasus does love a good show.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: Invitations are rare. The other way is the Star Passage, earned, never bought.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: Careful - a Passage duelist starts with a single star. Do not expect a warm welcome.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: A hooded courier hands out the Passage, only at night. Wait on the plaza bench.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got the card Magician of Faith from Simon.
pages.label: Reward

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Sit on the plaza bench and wait for night.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: Your hands shook, but your eyes did not. Rest and try again.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: The bench in the plaza. Be patient, {name}. The courier comes when the sun is gone.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: Lost, Won, Given. I know that riddle. Do not think of them as chores.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: Think of them as a mirror. The Kingdom will ask you the same three things.

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Simon sent you to sit on a bench? Hehe. Take a cushion, the stone is cold.

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: A bench? That's the plan? I thought it'd be more... dramatic. Good luck!

pages.speaker: guard
pages.text: Sitting outside after dark? I did not see anything. I was napping.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: A nice stone bench. It is not the time to sit yet.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: I'll sit here and wait. Surely the courier will show up any minute.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The sun sinks. The stalls close. The plaza grows quiet and cold.
pages.label: Later

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Nobody yet...

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: On a far rooftop, a robed figure stands in a faint green shimmer.
pages.label: Far Away

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Somebody is watching me from up there... Gone. Only a flicker of green.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Wait. Is someone standing by the old palm?

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Talk to the hooded man in the plaza.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: A good bench. When I come back a champion, I'll sit here and tell everyone.

pages.speaker: hooded_man
pages.text: You wait well. Few people do.

pages.speaker: hooded_man
pages.text: And ignore the one on the roof. He only watches. He never touches.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Who is he?

pages.speaker: hooded_man
pages.text: A reader, not a writer. Not tonight. Now, to business.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Are you the courier? Do you have the Star Passage?

pages.speaker: hooded_man
pages.text: I am a voice in the dark, nothing more. The Passage is not given. It is earned.

pages.speaker: hooded_man
pages.text: Take this card. It has three empty stamps.

pages.speaker: hooded_man
pages.text: Fill them with three treasures of your village. One lost. One won. One given.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: That is a riddle, not a quest!

pages.speaker: hooded_man
pages.text: Life is mostly riddles. Come to the harbor when the card is full. The ship won't wait long.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got the Stamp Card. It shows three empty stamps.
pages.label: You got

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The sun rises and the village wakes. Three treasures await.
pages.label: Next Morning

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Find a Lost, a Won and a Given treasure. Ask the villagers.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: baker
pages.text: Fresh bread! Warm bread! ... Nobody? Everyone is too busy whispering to eat.

pages.speaker: baker
pages.text: Mark my words - this Festival is cursed. Or very strange.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Hakim, do you know of any lost treasure around here?

pages.speaker: baker
pages.text: Funny you ask. My grandfather told me about one - the Founder's Scarab.

pages.speaker: baker
pages.text: It fell into the old cistern under the little pyramid, long ago.

pages.speaker: baker
pages.text: Last week I saw a pale light in the hatch. Brrr! Ask Kemet for his lantern.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Win Kemet's lantern, then open the hatch of the little pyramid.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Hakim, Teana needs honey for her festival cakes.

pages.speaker: baker
pages.text: For Teana's cakes? Of course! Here, careful, it is very sticky.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got a Honey Jar.
pages.label: You got

pages.speaker: baker
pages.text: Between batches I like a duel. Want to try your deck against my oven? Duel?

pages.speaker: baker
pages.text: Ha! You duel better than I bake. Here, a little thank-you.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got the card Mooyan Curry.
pages.label: Reward

pages.speaker: baker
pages.text: My bread rises faster than your deck. Try again!

pages.speaker: baker
pages.text: Safe travels, {name}. I'll keep a loaf warm for when you return.

pages.speaker: farmer
pages.text: Whispers? I'm a farmer. I mostly hear crickets and my goat.

pages.speaker: farmer
pages.text: My dates are ripe, though. Best dates for miles.

pages.speaker: farmer
pages.text: Dates ripe, sun hot, goat missing. That's my news.

pages.speaker: farmer
pages.text: I own the best lantern in the village, but I only lend it to the brave.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Hakim says you have a lantern. I need to go into the little pyramid.

pages.speaker: farmer
pages.text: Into the haunted hatch? Ha! Brave or crazy?

pages.speaker: farmer
pages.text: I only lend to the brave. Prove it with a duel! Duel?

pages.speaker: farmer
pages.text: Ha! Brave AND crazy. The best kind. Take the lantern.

pages.speaker: farmer
pages.text: And this card. If you hear music down there, run.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got a Lantern and the card Killer Needle.
pages.label: Reward

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Open the hatch of the little pyramid next to the house.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: farmer
pages.text: The lantern stays with me, friend. Practice and come back.

pages.speaker: farmer
pages.text: Mind the ghost. If you hear music, run. I said that already? Run anyway.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: A little pyramid with a stone hatch. It is far too dark to go inside.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Lantern lit. Down the old steps I go. Brrr, it's cold down here.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Up the steps and back into the warm sun.

pages.speaker: bakura
pages.text: A visitor! A real, breathing visitor! Oh, joyful day!

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Um... you are floating.

pages.speaker: bakura
pages.text: Three hundred years of floating. I walk through walls, but nobody ever drops by.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: I'm looking for the Founder's Scarab.

pages.speaker: bakura
pages.text: That shiny thing? I use it as a lamp! Win it from me. A duel! Please! Duel?

pages.speaker: bakura
pages.text: Splendid! The best duel in three centuries. Also the only one.

pages.speaker: bakura
pages.text: Take the Scarab. I'll find another lamp. Please visit again, it gets quiet.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got the Founder's Scarab and the card The 13th Grave.
pages.label: Reward

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A stamp glows on your Stamp Card - Lost.
pages.label: Stamp

pages.speaker: bakura
pages.text: Leaving already? Stay! One more duel? Pretty please?

pages.speaker: bakura
pages.text: Hello, friend! The step is slippery. Oh, and thank you for the visit.

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: ROAR! Behold the mighty Rex Raptor, wandering dinosaur duelist!

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Aren't you just passing through?

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: I collect trophies. See this bandana? Won it from a loud kid called Jono.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Jono's bandana... I should talk to him first.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Rex, I want Jono's bandana back.

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: Ha! Then take it from my dinosaurs. Win and it is yours. Fair is fair.

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: But lose, and I get your lucky socks too! Duel?

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: Impossible! My dinosaurs! My trophy!

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: Hmph. Take it. And this card, rookie. I don't carry grudges. Only dinosaurs.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got Jono's Bandana and the card Uraby.
pages.label: Reward

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A stamp glows on your Stamp Card - Won.
pages.label: Stamp

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: ROAR! More dinosaurs than you can count! Come back stronger.

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: I'll find a new trophy. You should enter that Kingdom, kid. I hear stars are shiny.

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: Ugh. {name}. Don't look at me. Worst day ever.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: What happened?

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: Rex Raptor, the big dino guy on the east road, bet my lucky bandana. I lost in three turns!

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: I'm too embarrassed to go back. If you won it back for me, I'd owe you big.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Beat Rex Raptor on the east road and win the bandana back.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: Rex is on the east road. Please be gentle... no, be MEAN.

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: My bandana! You did it! You actually did it!

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: It's yours. Take it.

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: No way. You won it fair and square. Keep it, it brings luck.

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: Take this card too. I have a plan, by the way. A secret plan. Heh.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got the card Dragon Treasure from Jono.
pages.label: Reward

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: That bandana looks better on you. Well, no. But keep it anyway.

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: {name}! You were out all night. Did the ghost bite you? Hehe.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: I'm looking for a Given treasure. Whatever that means.

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Given? Oh... I can't talk now. The festival starts and I have no cakes!

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: I need honey from Hakim, fresh river water and ripe dates. But I can't leave the stall.

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Help me and I'll give you something precious. Here, take my water jug.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got a Water Jug.
pages.label: You got

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Get honey from Hakim, fill the jug at the river, pick dates from a palm.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Honey from Hakim, water from the river and dates from a palm. Please hurry!

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Honey, water AND dates! You're a hero, {name}!

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: The cakes need time to bake. So duel me! I want my charm in good hands.

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: If you win, the charm is yours. If you lose, you wash dishes! Duel?

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Wow! Okay, okay, you win. A deal is a deal.

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: This is my Lucky Charm. My granny gave it to me. I can't go anywhere, but you can.

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: It is not a trade. It is a gift. That is what makes it special.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got the Lucky Charm and the card Kuriboh.
pages.label: Reward

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A stamp glows on your Stamp Card - Given.
pages.label: Stamp

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Hehe, I won! Dishes after the festival. Try again, {name}!

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Come and see me before you go, ok? And take care of that charm.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: The palm is full of ripe dates. Shake, shake, shake!

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Plop, plop, plop! A whole basket of sweet dates.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got Dates.
pages.label: You got

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Ripe dates. Teana would love some. Maybe I should ask her first.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: The river is cool and clear. Glug, glug, glug.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got River Water.
pages.label: You got

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: A clear river. The fish stare at me as if I owe them money.

pages.speaker: guard
pages.text: Orders - nobody crosses the bridge today. Not after that poster business.

pages.speaker: guard
pages.text: Unless you have a very good reason. And a very full card.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: The Guard blocks the bridge. I can't cross yet.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: The Stamp Card is full! Lost, Won and Given, all three stamps are glowing.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: The hooded man said to come to the harbor. The road is across the bridge.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Cross the bridge to the harbor. The Guard will let you pass.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: guard
pages.text: That glowing card... is that a full Star Passage card? In twenty years I never saw one!

pages.speaker: guard
pages.text: Go on. The bridge is yours. Be careful, {name}.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Across the bridge and down the golden road. I smell salt in the air.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Creaking ropes and gulls. A gate, and an empty pier beyond it.
pages.label: The Harbor

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Back across the bridge, to the village.

pages.speaker: soldier
pages.text: Halt, traveler. This pier is closed for the Kingdom ship.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: I have a Stamp Card with three stamps.

pages.speaker: soldier
pages.text: Impressive. But anyone can collect stamps. Duelists must pass the Harbor Exam.

pages.speaker: soldier
pages.text: Beat me and the gate opens. Lose and go practice. Duel?

pages.speaker: soldier
pages.text: Excellent! The gate is open. The Courier is waiting at the end of the pier.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got the card Warrior of Tradition.
pages.label: Reward

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Walk to the end of the pier and meet the Courier.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: soldier
pages.text: Not today. Go practice and come back, recruit.

pages.speaker: soldier
pages.text: Go ahead, the pier is waiting. Good luck over the sea.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: The gate is shut. The Inspector stands right in front of it.

pages.speaker: shadi
pages.text: You came. I am Shadi, Pegasus's messenger. And yes, I was the hooded man.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: I knew that voice was familiar!

pages.speaker: shadi
pages.text: You did not. Do not lie to a spirit. The three stamps - Memory, Courage, Kindness.

pages.speaker: shadi
pages.text: A duelist needs all three. And a deck. One last test - duel me. Duel?

pages.speaker: shadi
pages.text: Your cards are loyal and your heart is true. The Star Passage is yours.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: On the far breakwater, a robed figure glows green and looks at your Star Passage.
pages.label: Far Away

pages.speaker: shadi
pages.text: Hm. Someone has read your Passage. Ignore him. He only reads.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Who is 'he'?

pages.speaker: shadi
pages.text: A reader. He never turns a page for you. Back to your Passage.

pages.speaker: shadi
pages.text: Invited duelists enter with three stars. Passage duelists enter with only one.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: One star? That is hardly anything!

pages.speaker: shadi
pages.text: It is all you need to begin. Win a duel, take a star. Lose and one goes. At zero, you go home.

pages.speaker: shadi
pages.text: Before each star duel you pick the wager. Lose, and your rival keeps it.

pages.speaker: shadi
pages.text: If your last star is lost, there is no camp and no second chance. Your journey ends there.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Game over, then. I will never bet my last star lightly.

pages.speaker: shadi
pages.text: Ten stars open the castle. Pegasus waits at the top. Your friends came to see you off.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got the Star Passage, a Star Chip and the card Illusionist Faceless Mage.
pages.label: Reward

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You have 1 star. The white ship arrives at the pier.
pages.label: Stars

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Say goodbye to Simon, Teana and Jono, then board the ship.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: shadi
pages.text: Your heart is willing but your deck needs work. Try again, young one.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: So the ship is real. I'm too old for sea voyages, but my heart sails with you.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: I must confess something. Who do you think wrote to Pegasus?

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: YOU did?!

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: Pegasus and I were friends once. We argued about cards. He built an island, I built a village.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: He asked for my best student. I said I'd think about it. Then you showed up with that deck.

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: Tell him Simon says hello. And that he still owes me a card. Take this one, my first.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got the card Mystical Elf from Simon.
pages.label: Reward

pages.speaker: simon
pages.text: Go. And remember - stars are only numbers. Cards are only paper. People matter.

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Take care! I'm not crying, it's the sea breeze! Bring back a BIG story.

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: I'll keep my golden star safe until you're back. Don't lose that charm!

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Go on, before I start crying for real. Hehe.

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: So you got the Passage! Of course you did. Heh.

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: Don't think I'm giving up. I have a raft, three barrels and a dream.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Jono, you can't swim.

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: Details! See you on the island, {name}!

pages.speaker: jono
pages.text: Raft, barrels, dream. Easy. Go, I'll catch up!

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: My friends are still here. I should say goodbye before I leave.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A horn blows. A white ship with a golden eye on its sail waits at the pier.
pages.label: All Aboard

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Goodbye, home town. I'll be back with stories.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Look around the ship and talk to the lady on deck.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: Well, well. A rookie from the sand. Cute. Where are your friends?

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: I came alone. I think. Who are you?

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: Mai Valentine. Harpie Ladies and bad manners. Let me guess - Passage, one star?

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: Oh sweetie. Here are the rules so you don't cry later. Win a duel, take one star.

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: Lose a duel, give one up. Zone masters are worth two stars. Ten stars open the castle.

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: No stars left? Pegasus's men send you home. Do not let that happen.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Thanks for the tips.

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: Don't thank me. We'll duel soon. And I won't go easy on you.

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: Look at the sea. Last time you can enjoy it before the fun starts.

pages.speaker: inseto
pages.text: STOP RIGHT THERE, bug! Talk to the lady first. I want an audience.

pages.speaker: inseto
pages.text: HAHAHA! Look at all these little bugs crawling onto MY ship!

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Who are you calling a bug? And it's not your ship.

pages.speaker: inseto
pages.text: I am InsetoKaiba! Champion! Bug collector! Owner of the most unbeatable deck ever made!

pages.speaker: inseto
pages.text: Nobody has ever touched it. Not once. I checked. Twice.

pages.speaker: inseto
pages.text: Face me, little larva, and learn your place in the food chain. Duel?

pages.speaker: inseto
pages.text: WHAT?! Impossible! I am InsetoKaiba! My deck is UNBEATABLE!

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: It was beatable. Just now.

pages.speaker: inseto
pages.text: A glitch! A bug in the system! ... And I am the only bug allowed here!

pages.speaker: inseto
pages.text: Fine. Take this, you mildly impressive beetle. I will remember your name.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got the Golden Bug Pin and the card Javelin Beetle.
pages.label: Reward

pages.speaker: inseto
pages.text: HAHAHA! Squashed! Another bug for my collection! Come back when you grow wings, larva.

pages.speaker: inseto
pages.text: You again? Shoo, shoo! I'm rehearsing my victory speech. It is very long.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: A barrel on the deck. It smells like... date cakes?

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The barrel whispers - 'Shhh...' and giggles.
pages.label: Barrel

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: The sea is wide. Maybe I should talk to the lady on deck first.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: At the top of the mast, a robed figure sits in a green shimmer, watching the island.
pages.label: Up High

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Mai, who is that up on the mast?

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: Where? Nobody is up there, sweetie. Too much sun.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The green flicker goes out. The mast is empty.
pages.label: Up High

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The mist parts. Towers, flags and a castle with a giant eye on its tallest spire.
pages.label: Mist

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Duelist Kingdom. One star. Ten to go. Let's play.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Chapter 2 - The Shore of Illusions
pages.label: End of Chapter 1

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Green characters flicker on the wall, like a window into something else.
pages.label: Wall

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: I can't read it. Something like 'observe... do not edit'.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The glyphs fade. Nothing in the room has changed.
pages.label: Wall

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Plain old stone. Whatever was written here has gone quiet.

pages.speaker: bakura
pages.text: The green writing on the wall? It was here before me.

pages.speaker: bakura
pages.text: It never helps and never harms. It only watches. I like it. Good company.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Hello! I am Nabil. No title, really. I just enjoy teaching new duelists.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: This patch of sand is my Duel Academy. Tuition is free and shoes are optional.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Five short classes, then a practice duel. Come back for each new class.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Class unlocked - turns, cards and battle.
pages.label: Duel Academy

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Class one - the rhythm of a duel. Both duelists begin with 8000 Life Points.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Your hand refills to five each turn. You must play one card or one ordered combination.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: There are no tributes here. A monster you just played can attack on that same turn.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Each upright monster may attack once per turn. You choose the order of those attacks.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Attack upright. Turn sideways to defend. Press Start to end your turn.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: With no enemy monster, you attack Life Points directly. Empty them and you win.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Complete. Next class - Guardian Stars.
pages.label: Class 1

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Each monster offers two Guardian Stars. Choose one when you summon it.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Mars beats Jupiter, then Saturn, Uranus, Pluto, Neptune, then Mars.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Second cycle - Mercury beats Sun, Sun beats Moon, Moon beats Venus, and Venus beats Mercury.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Only neighbors in the same cycle matter. Advantage swings the battle by 500 points.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Check the enemy star before attacking. A weaker monster can win with the right Guardian.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Complete. Next class - fields and terrain.
pages.label: Class 2

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: A field card changes the terrain for both duelists until another field replaces it.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: A favored type gains 500 ATK and DEF. A harmed type loses 500 ATK and DEF.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Forest helps Beasts, Beast-Warriors, Insects and Plants.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Mountain helps Dragons, Winged Beasts and Thunder monsters.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Wasteland helps Zombies, Dinosaurs and Rocks. Sogen helps Warriors and Beast-Warriors.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Umi helps sea types, Aqua and Thunder, but hurts Machines and Pyro monsters.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Yami helps Spellcasters and Fiends, but hurts Fairies. A field can help your rival too.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Complete. Next class - raising ATK and DEF.
pages.label: Class 3

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Equip cards fit only certain monsters. Combine a valid equip with its monster to use it.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Most equips add 500 ATK and DEF. Megamorph adds 1000. Several equips can stack.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: You may combine them in your hand or play one onto your monster already on the field.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: An invalid equip is discarded. Test safely, and remember which monsters accept each one.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Equip and terrain bonuses stack. Guardian advantage adds its own 500 during battle.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Complete. Next class - wild fusions.
pages.label: Class 4

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Now the fun part. In your hand, press Up to number two or more cards in order.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Confirm. The first two combine. Their survivor meets the third, then the next.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Some recipes are exact. Many use types and strength. Dragon plus Thunder is a famous path.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: If two monsters fail to fuse, the first is lost and the second stays. Order matters a lot.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: You can also play a card onto your field monster to fuse or equip it in the same zone.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Experiment. The strangest chains often turn a weak hand into one enormous monster.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Complete. Return for Nabil's practice duel.
pages.label: Class 5

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: You know turns, Guardians, fields, equips and fusion chains. Time for the sand exam.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: My deck is simple. Try a fusion, watch the stars, and use the field if it favors you.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: No entry fee and no shame in losing. Ready for your practice duel?

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Excellent! You read the board instead of staring only at the biggest ATK number.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Academy complete. I will stay here if you want a summary and another practice duel.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Training complete. Professor Nabil remains available in the village.
pages.label: Duel Academy

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Good practice. A loss costs nothing here, and now you know where your plan broke.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Change one thing, not the whole deck. Then come back and try again.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Quick review - play one card or ordered chain, then battle and press Start to end.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Guardian advantage swings 500. Terrain changes ATK and DEF. Valid equips stack.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Fusion chains resolve in numbered order. A failed pair can discard the first card.

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: That is the whole academy. Want another practice duel?

pages.speaker: academy_teacher
pages.text: Sharp play. Class dismissed until you feel like shuffling again.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Sand, tents and a painted sign - Welcome, bugs and champions.
pages.label: Shore of Illusions

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: Off you go, sweetie. Keep that star warm. See you at the castle.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: A giant mirror in the middle of the beach? That is not normal.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Look into the mirror on the beach.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The glass ripples. A man in red with silver hair smiles out of it.
pages.label: Mirror

pages.speaker: pegasus
pages.text: Welcome, duelists, to my little Kingdom! This is only a recording.

pages.speaker: pegasus
pages.text: Every duelist carries stars. Before a duel you both wager. The winner takes the pot.

pages.speaker: pegasus
pages.text: Ten stars open my castle gate. Zero stars... nobody likes zero.

pages.speaker: pegasus
pages.text: Lose your last one and you are out of my Kingdom. Game over. No refunds.

pages.speaker: pegasus
pages.text: Now go and play! I will be watching. I am always watching.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Always watching? Creepy. One star. Let's find a duel.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Only your own face now, and a faint smell of strawberry jam.
pages.label: Mirror

pages.speaker: weevil
pages.text: Hihihi! A rookie with one shiny little star. How lucky for me.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Who are you? And why were you hiding behind a palm tree?

pages.speaker: weevil
pages.text: Weevil Underwood, champion of bugs! Let's roll to see who starts.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Weevil rolls. Six. He rolls again. Six. And again. Six.
pages.label: Dice

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Those dice are loaded! Every face is a six!

pages.speaker: weevil
pages.text: Prove it. Duel me for your star, or walk away and cry.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Beat Weevil on the beach. Each of you wagers a star.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: weevil
pages.text: I hold two stars. Bet what you dare. Winner takes it. Loser cries. Hihihi!

pages.speaker: weevil
pages.text: Well? My bugs are hungry. Duel?

pages.speaker: weevil
pages.text: Impossible! My bugs! My dice! My beautiful plan!

pages.speaker: weevil
pages.text: Take your star. And these dice. They never liked me anyway.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: You got a star, the Loaded Dice and the card Hercules Beetle.
pages.label: Reward

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Two stars. Eight to go. Note to self - bring my own dice.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Next - the Forest of Whispers, up the jungle path.
pages.label: End of Chapter 2

pages.speaker: weevil
pages.text: Hihihi! Your star is mine. Bugs always win in the end.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: I'll get stronger. New cards, then a rematch. No loaded dice.

pages.speaker: weevil
pages.text: Go away. The dice and I are not speaking.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: You still hold the stars you took from me. I want them back. Duel?

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Cots, a fire and a sign - Lost your stars? Rest here.
pages.label: Shore Camp

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Fine print - Zero stars means the end of your journey. No star is ever given back.
pages.label: Shore Camp

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: No safety net. Then I never bet my last star.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The fire crackles. A few eliminated duelists snore.
pages.label: Shore Camp

pages.speaker: hooded_man
pages.text: The Kingdom tests more than decks. Watch who collects the stars.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A gust of sand. The end of the pier is empty again.
pages.label: Pier

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A sign - Forest of Whispers. Duelists with two stars only.
pages.label: Jungle Path

pages.speaker: dock_dan
pages.text: Fresh off the boat! Cards, cheap. Well, cheap-ish.

pages.speaker: purser
pages.text: Snacks, cards and seasick pills. Only the cards work.

pages.speaker: shell_sue
pages.text: Shells, cards and secrets. Buy something, star boy.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Two stars glow on your glove. The sign lets you pass.
pages.label: Jungle Path

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Forest of Whispers. If the trees start talking, I'm leaving.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The path climbs back into the whispering trees.
pages.label: Jungle Path

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The trees thin out. You smell the sea again.
pages.label: Forest Edge

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Leaves rustle with no wind. Something is cut into the bark.
pages.label: Forest of Whispers

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: A star... carved into the tree. Fresh cut. Someone was here.

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: THIS WAY? NO! THAT WAY! Stupid trees keep moving!

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: That shouting sounds familiar. Rex Raptor, from home?

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Find the duelist shouting in the forest.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: You! The kid from the village! Did you move the trees?

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Trees don't move, Rex. You're lost. Since when?

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: Since breakfast! My dinos are hungry and so am I. Star on the line!

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: One star each, then. And after that I show you the way out.

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: Deal! Duel me right now, star for star?

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: Extinct... again. Fine. Take the star. You earned it.

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: I saw those carved stars. Three of them. They point somewhere.

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: I followed them in circles. You try. I'm going to eat a mushroom.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A star and the card Megazowler.
pages.label: You got

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Follow the three Star Marks on the trees.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: HA! Rawr! Still got it! Now which way is out?

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Ugh. My deck needs bigger teeth. The forest shop, maybe.

pages.speaker: rex
pages.text: This mushroom tastes like socks. Go follow your stars.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A star cut deep in the bark. One point aims east.
pages.label: Star Mark

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: One. The cut is clean, like a chisel. Not an animal.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Another star, higher up. Its point aims at the stone gate.
pages.label: Star Mark

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Two. Whoever carves these is tall. Or brought a ladder.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A third star, still sticky with sap. It points to the gate too.
pages.label: Star Mark

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Three. Same hand. Same star. Who is marking this island?

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The carved star. You already followed this one.
pages.label: Star Mark

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Old stones and a cold blue glow. It will not let you in.
pages.label: Stone Gate

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The three stars glow at once. The gate hums and the mist parts.
pages.label: Stone Gate

pages.speaker: forest_mage
pages.text: Three stars read, three steps true. The clearing welcomes you.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: You carved them? The stars on the trees?

pages.speaker: forest_mage
pages.text: Not I. They appear each moon. I only guard where they point.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Duel the Forest Mage at the stone gate.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: forest_mage
pages.text: I am the master of this wood. Three stars sleep in my roots.

pages.speaker: forest_mage
pages.text: Wager what you dare. The forest is fair. Its roots are not.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: One more star makes four. Let's grow some.

pages.speaker: forest_mage
pages.text: Then draw, sprout. Shall the roots begin?

pages.speaker: forest_mage
pages.text: The roots bow. Take my star, and this leaf.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A star, the Whisper Leaf and the card Mystic Horseman.
pages.label: You got

pages.speaker: forest_mage
pages.text: Whoever carves the stars walks every zone. Ask the mountains.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Four stars. Ten open the castle. A long way yet.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The Forest of Whispers is behind you. The mountain pass waits.
pages.label: End of Chapter 3

pages.speaker: forest_mage
pages.text: Roots hold. Come back with a stronger deck, little sprout.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Hermit Hob's hut and the Hollow Log Ring. Time to train.

pages.speaker: forest_mage
pages.text: The leaf will whisper when a star is near. Listen to it.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A rope bars the road - Zone master's leave required.
pages.label: Mountain Pass

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The rope stays tight. The pass lets in only duelists with four stars.
pages.label: Mountain Pass

pages.speaker: hermit_hob
pages.text: Mushrooms, moss and cards. The cards are the least weird.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Four stars glow on your glove. The rope falls away.
pages.label: Mountain Pass

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Up we go. The castle has to be somewhere above the clouds.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The road climbs back into the rocks and the wind.
pages.label: Mountain Road

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The wind drops. Pine smell. The forest is below.
pages.label: Pine Trail

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A chasm splits the pass. One rope bridge. One man on it.
pages.label: Mountain Pass

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Another star cut in the rock, up by that cave. Bigger this time.

pages.speaker: keith
pages.text: Toll bridge, kid! Nobody crosses Bandit Keith for free.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Talk to the man guarding the rope bridge.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: keith
pages.text: House rules. I got three stars in the pot. Bet what you got. Win, you cross.

pages.speaker: keith
pages.text: You lose, your stars stay with me. Lose 'em all and you're done for good. Fair, huh?

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Fair for you. That deck smells like rigged slot machines.

pages.speaker: keith
pages.text: In America we call it strategy. Shuffle up or scram?

pages.speaker: keith
pages.text: Tch. Machines jammed. Here, my star. And this junk.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A star and the card Pendulum Machine.
pages.label: You got

pages.speaker: keith
pages.text: Blondie's waiting on the other side. She's no pushover.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Cross the rope bridge.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: keith
pages.text: Jackpot! Thanks for the star, kid. Bridge stays closed.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: His machines hit hard. Cliff Cass's tent, or the mine pit.

pages.speaker: keith
pages.text: Beat it. I'm counting chips. Bridge is yours, sucker.

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: Took you long enough. I was starting to like the view.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Mai! You came up the pass alone? Keith let you through?

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: Keith owed me. You owe me a duel. No stars, just pride.

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: Show me the ship wasn't luck. Ready, kid?

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: Not bad. My ladies needed a lesson in humility.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The card Harpie Lady. Mai keeps her star.
pages.label: You got

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: Free tip. Someone taps stone in that cave every night.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Find who carves the stars in the cave.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: Pretty cards, weak hand. Come back when you've grown.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: She wasn't kidding. I need sky cards. The mine pit has them.

pages.speaker: mai
pages.text: Go on, detective. The cave. I'll keep the view.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A huge star cut over the mouth. Inside, only cold and dark.
pages.label: Star Cave

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Tap. Tap. A hooded man is chiseling a star into the wall.
pages.label: Star Cave

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Got you! The beach, the forest, here. You carve the stars!

pages.speaker: croquet
pages.text: Ahem. Croquet, steward of Master Pegasus. Guilty.

pages.speaker: croquet
pages.text: Each star is a window. The Master watches who walks by.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: He's been watching me since the shore? Why me?

pages.speaker: croquet
pages.text: He watches everyone. You he watches... closely. Good day.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The Star Chisel he left behind.
pages.label: You got

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Climb to the summit gate.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Only stone dust and the fresh star. He is long gone.
pages.label: Star Cave

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A stone arch in the clouds. Six stars are carved on it. The wind pushes you back.
pages.label: Summit Gate

pages.speaker: mountain_mage
pages.text: Few reach the summit with five stars. Fewer leave with six.

pages.speaker: mountain_mage
pages.text: Four stars rest on this summit. Wager as many as your nerve allows.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Ten stars open the castle. I'm not going back down now.

pages.speaker: mountain_mage
pages.text: Then stand firm, pebble. Shall the stone speak?

pages.speaker: mountain_mage
pages.text: The stone cracks. My star, and my stone soldier.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A star and the card Giant Soldier of Stone.
pages.label: You got

pages.speaker: mountain_mage
pages.text: Croquet came this way too. The castle knows you are coming.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Six stars. Four to go, and a host watching every step.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The Mountain Pass is behind you. The castle road opens.
pages.label: End of Chapter 4

pages.speaker: mountain_mage
pages.text: Pebbles roll back down. Return heavier, little one.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Stone beats me. Cliff Cass and the Mine Shaft Pit, then.

pages.speaker: mountain_mage
pages.text: The road beyond the arch is yours. Mind the eyes on it.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Hedges and flowers open beyond the arch. The Meadow Maze waits.
pages.label: Castle Road

pages.speaker: cliff_cass
pages.text: Rope, pitons, cards. Only the cards ever save anyone.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A tarp, a cot and a lantern. Kingdom staff keep it lit.
pages.label: Trail Camp

pages.speaker: staff
pages.text: Careful up there. Nobody here gives stars back. Lose your last and your journey is over.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Six stars. The wind turns soft. Hedges and flowers.
pages.label: Meadow Maze

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: A maze. After the pass, this almost feels like a break.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The hedges close in again. Flower smell. Soft ground.
pages.label: Meadow Road

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The wind turns hard. Stone underfoot. The pass is above.
pages.label: Summit Trail

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Tall green walls. Paths that twist. Someone giggles in the leaves.
pages.label: Meadow Maze

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: That laugh. I heard it inside a barrel on the ship.

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Shh! You found me. Surprise!

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Talk to Teana in the hedges.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: I hid in that barrel. The ship smelled like fish and adventure!

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Teana! The village is going to miss you. And the cakes.

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: I brought a golden star. The hooded man gave it to me. Look - same shape as yours!

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Duel me first. Friendly. If you win, I guide you through the maze. Deal?

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Ow, my pride! Fine. You win. I am your maze guide now.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Teana's Hint Charm. She will tip you from here on.
pages.label: You got

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Centre of the maze: a mage with stars. She does not giggle. Go careful.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Find the Meadow Mage at the maze centre.
pages.label: Objective

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Hee! Still got it. Try again when you are ready. I will wait.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: She plays cute and hits hard. Rose Rue's cart, or the rabbit hole.

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: Left, left, right, then the star stone. Or ask me again. I like talking.

pages.speaker: teana
pages.text: The Mage holds stars. Bet small if you want the curve. Bet big if you are brave. Or broke.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A carved star in the stone. The hedges still feel closed.
pages.label: Star Stone

pages.speaker: meadow_mage
pages.text: Six stars walk my maze. Few leave with seven.

pages.speaker: meadow_mage
pages.text: Two stars rest in these hedges. Wager what your nerve allows.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Ten open the castle. I am not turning back for flowers.

pages.speaker: meadow_mage
pages.text: Then bloom or wilt, traveler. Shall the meadow speak?

pages.speaker: meadow_mage
pages.text: The hedges part. My star, and a leaf from my crown.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A star and the card Queen of Autumn Leaves.
pages.label: You got

pages.speaker: meadow_mage
pages.text: Beyond the arch the grass turns gold. Desert wind. The Kingdom still watches.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: Seven stars. Three to go. Teana is humming somewhere in the leaves.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: The Meadow Maze is behind you. The desert road opens.
pages.label: End of Chapter 5

pages.speaker: meadow_mage
pages.text: Petals fall. Return heavier, little bloom.

pages.speaker: atos
pages.text: She outplayed me. Rose Rue and the Rabbit Hole Ring, then.

pages.speaker: meadow_mage
pages.text: The arch is yours. Mind the thorns on the way.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Gold grass. Hot wind. Chapter 6 arrives in the next part.
pages.label: Desert Road

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A vine-covered arch. Seven stars are carved on it. The hedges push you back.
pages.label: Desert Arch

pages.speaker: rose_rue
pages.text: Roses, thorns and cards. Only the cards ever bloom twice.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: A tarp among wildflowers. Kingdom staff keep a lantern lit.
pages.label: Meadow Camp

pages.speaker: staff
pages.text: Pretty place. Deadly rules. Lose your last star and your journey ends for good.
